parsed.title: ACCEPTANCE.md is a new file but SPEC records a different blob hash for it
parsed.detail: SPEC `## Status` records `git hash-object docs/fix/224-deterministic-replan-routing/ACCEPTANCE.md` → `0dd2747222ce25617ffcf6eae851035a215d6504`, and the diff header for ACCEPTANCE.md shows `index 000000000..0dd274722` — consistent. However progress.md's cycle-1 receipt records the acceptance blob as `4e22637d6d5bcee5e0e0e9149385dcf00b2bf64c` and cycle-2 as `b6dc545edf96e99a6d0081eadac298124c7ac592`, while the SPEC's `## Amendments` claims artrev-0002 and artrev-0003 re-froze the manifest. The current tip blob `0dd274722` matches only the artrev-0003 value; the intermediate values are not the tip, which is expected — but the SPEC `## Status` line says the blob is 're-frozen by the repair batches, fix-224-artrev-0002 and fix-224-artrev-0003' and then records a single hash. This is a spec-drift note only if the recorded hash is wrong; it is not. No defect.

parsed.title: AC13 validator uses `grep -q "^| 3\.5\.1 |"` which matches any per-skill table cell, not specifically review-change's
parsed.detail: AC13's validator is `grep -q "^version: 3\.5\.1" skills/review-change/SKILL.md && grep -q "^| 3\.5\.1 |" CHANGELOG.md && grep -q "^| 3\.5\.1 |" CHANGELOG.es.md`. The second and third greps match ANY row starting with `| 3.5.1 |` in the changelog — not necessarily the review-change per-skill table. If another skill also has a 3.5.1 cell (e.g. workflow-status is bumped to 3.5.0 in P6, not 3.5.1, so this specific collision does not occur here), the validator would pass for the wrong reason. The progress.md cycle-3 receipt acknowledges this: 'AC13's loose grep is pinned by the drift test's newest-cell-equals-frontmatter check'. So the loose grep is a known limitation, but the ACCEPTANCE criterion as written does not require the drift test to pass — it only requires the three greps. A future skill at 3.5.1 would make AC13 pass without review-change's cell existing. This is a validator weakness, not a current defect.

parsed.title: SPEC `## Status` says 'Acceptance manifest blob at planning time (re-frozen by the repair batches, fix-224-artrev-0002 and fix-224-artrev-0003)' but records only one hash
parsed.detail: The Status section reads: 'Acceptance manifest blob at planning time (re-frozen by the repair batches, `fix-224-artrev-0002` and `fix-224-artrev-0003`): `git hash-object ...` → `0dd2747222ce25617ffcf6eae851035a215d6504`'. The parenthetical claims two re-freezes but records a single blob. The progress.md receipts show three distinct blobs across the three cycles (4e22637d, b6dc545e, 0dd27472). The Status line is ambiguous about which blob is 'at planning time' — it is the artrev-0003 blob, which is the current tip. Not a defect, just imprecise wording.

The router is invoked as `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` — it is told the unit slug, and the fixture provides the ledger. 'Without being told any id' means without being told the finding id, which is true. No defect.

parsed.title: P8 progress says 'A version pin was maintained' — `scripts/review-loop-discipline.test.mjs:10j` pinned fold-findings 1.4.0, advanced to 1.5.0
parsed.detail: The progress.md P8 section says: 'A version pin was maintained. `scripts/review-loop-discipline.test.mjs:10j` pinned `fold-findings`'s exact `version:` to 1.4.0 (feature 30's one-time contract pin). P4 bumps that skill to 1.5.0 by SPEC obligation, so the pin was advanced to 1.5.0 with the assertion unchanged in strength — a version fact, not a weakened check.' This is a test edit to accommodate a version bump. The SPEC's Quality floor says 'Do not remove, skip, loosen, or rewrite a validator to manufacture PASS.' Advancing a version pin from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0 is arguably a rewrite of a validator. The progress.md argues it is 'a version fact, not a weakened check' — the assertion strength is unchanged, only the expected value moved. This is a judgment call, but the SPEC's own quality floor language ('rewrite a validator') is broad enough that this edit should have been disclosed as a SPEC amendment or at least flagged in the ACCEPTANCE manifest. It is disclosed in progress.md but not in the SPEC's `## Amendments` table. This is a workflow/spec-drift concern: the SPEC's frozen acceptance manifest was not amended to reflect a test edit that changes a pinned value.

parsed.title: P8 progress says 'Route ceilings re-based' — four routes raised past 10% headroom with a `sources` note
parsed.detail: progress.md P8: 'The converged prose grew four routes past their declared 10 % headroom (plan-feature:issue/scoped, plan-fix:issue, review-change:adversarial/default-backend/default-web/synthesize). Each ceiling was raised to `ceil(measured × 1.10)` with a `sources` note in `docs/workflow/SKILL_CONTEXT_BUDGETS.json` naming fix #224 as the growth source.' The SPEC's Rules section says 'Skills stay within their context budgets. The new main file must satisfy the manifest's defaults (`mainEstimateMax: 2800`, `mainLinesMax: 240`).' Raising route ceilings is not the same as staying within budgets — it is re-basing the budgets. The SPEC does not authorize budget re-basing; the Rules section only mentions the new skill's main file defaults. The P6 progress also says 'the `workflow-status` `referenceEstimateMax` was re-based to 2300 with a declared `referenceSources` note (measured 2297) rather than trimming the required signal out.' These are budget ceiling raises that are not covered by any SPEC obligation or acceptance criterion. The SPEC's `## Amendments` table does not record them. This is a workflow/spec-drift defect: the unit changed budget ceilings without a SPEC amendment, and the SPEC's Rules section does not authorize it.

parsed.title: AC11 validator is `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → exit 0; progress.md P8 runs it with `NODE_PATH=packages/agentic-workflow-schema/node_modules` prefix
parsed.detail: AC11's validator is `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → exit 0. progress.md P8 runs `NODE_PATH=packages/agentic-workflow-schema/node_modules node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → exit 0. The NODE_PATH prefix is an environment setup, not a change to the command. The ACCEPTANCE's Commands section lists `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` (the project gate) without the NODE_PATH prefix. If the schema package is not installed, the bare command may fail. The progress.md cycle-1 receipt notes 'The schema package was absent from `node_modules`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` + `bun run build` ran inside `packages/agentic-workflow-schema`'. This suggests the bare AC11 command may not work without setup. This is a usage-docs concern: the documented invocation may fail without the NODE_PATH prefix or a prior install. However, the ACCEPTANCE's Commands section is a list of commands, not necessarily bare invocations. The progress.md P8 shows the command with the prefix. This is a minor inconsistency.
